Then John states that Jesus “breathed on them, and saith unto them, Receive ye the Holy Ghost” (v.22) - from Luke's account we know that this means that “opened he their understanding, that they might understand the scriptures” (Lk 24:45 KJV). Finally, Jesus says: “Whose soever sins ye remit, they are remitted unto them; and whose soever sins ye retain, they are retained” (v.23) - this is a very controversial verse since Roman Catholicism uses it to claim that Jesus gave the apostles (and their successors) the power and authority to forgive sins. But in view of the parallel passages, Luke gives clarity to the meaning of this verse: “that repentance and remission of sins should be preached in his name” (Lk 24:47 KJV) - hence, “to retain sin” is not withhold from sharing the gospel, and “to remit sin” is to preach the good news. After Jesus ascends into heaven, the disciples obey Jesus’ Great Commission, and Peter uses the “keys of heaven” for the first time in Acts 2:38: “Repent, and be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins, and ye shall receive the gift of the Holy Ghost” (Acts 2:38 KJV) - notice the singular name, and notice its purpose: Jesus, for the forgiveness of sins. This is the key to heaven which Peter shared in Acts 2:38.

The name invoked at baptism is “JESUS,” not a nameless vague Trinity. The Trinity describes the name of Jesus, not the other way around: “And now why tarriest thou? arise, and be baptized, and wash away thy sins, CALLING ON THE NAME OF THE LORD” (Acts 22:16 KJV) - notice the name of “JESUS”(the name of the Lord) is explicitly invoked at baptism. That’s why James 2:7 says: “Is it not they who slander and blaspheme that precious name(singular name) by which you are distinguished and called [the name of Christ invoked in baptism]?” (James 2:7 AMPC) or “Is it not they who blaspheme the honorable name(singular name) which was INVOKED OVER YOU?” (James 2:7 RSV). THE NAME IS ALWAYS “JESUS”: “Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the NAME(singular, only “Jesus” fulfills all three titles, you can see that in Isaiah 9:6) of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost” (Mt 28:19 KJV); “Go and make disciples of all the nations IN MY NAME(Jesus)” (Mt 28:19 as cited by Eusebius of Caesarea, Constantine’s historian, before the Council of Nicaea); “IN MY NAME(Jesus) shall they cast out devils; they shall speak with new tongues…” (Mk 16:17 KJV); “that repentance and remission of sins should be preached IN HIS NAME(Jesus) among all nations” (Lk 24:47 KJV); “Repent, and be baptized every one of you IN THE NAME OF JESUS CHRIST for the remission of sins” (Acts 2:38 KJV); “But when they believed Philip preaching the things concerning the kingdom of God, and THE NAME OF JESUS CHRIST, they were baptized, both men and women” (Acts 8:12 KJV); “...only they were baptized IN THE NAME OF THE LORD JESUS” (Acts 8:16 KJV); “And he commanded them TO BE BAPTIZED IN THE NAME OF THE LORD(Jesus)” (Acts 10:48 KJV); “When they heard this, they were baptized IN THE NAME OF THE LORD JESUS” (Acts 19:5 KJV) - Paul literally REBAPTIZED people so it could be done in Jesus’ name specifically(Acts 19:3-5); “Know ye not, that so many of us as were BAPTIZED INTO JESUS CHRIST were baptized into his death? Therefore we are BURIED with his BY BAPTISM into death…” (Rom 6:3-4 KJV) - notice how baptism is about Jesus’ death, not a vague, nameless Trinity, and notice how we are BURIED in water, not sprinkled like how the institutionalized religion does it; “Is Christ divided? was Paul crucified for you? or were ye baptized in the name of Paul?” (1 Cor 1:13 KJV) - no, they were not baptized in the name of Paul, they were baptized in the name of Jesus; “For as many of you as have been BAPTIZED INTO CHRIST have put on Christ” (Gal 3:27 KJV) - you are baptized into Christ, not into a Trinity; “Buried with HIM(Jesus) in baptism” (Col 2:12 KJV) - buried with HIM(Jesus), not a Trinity.

Col 2:9-10 says the fullness of the Godhead is in Jesus, and that we are COMPLETE in Him. Jesus declares the Father's name (Jn 17:26). Jesus manifested the Father's name (Jn 17:6). Who receives Jesus receives the Father (Jn 13:20). Who believes in Jesus believes in the Father (Jn 12:44). If you know Jesus you know the Father (Jn 8:19). Honoring the Son you honor the Father (Jn 5:23). We gather in the name of Jesus (Mt 18:20). Whatever we ask we ask in the name of Jesus (Jn 16:23). We pray and make requests in Jesus' name (Jn 14:13-14). We do signs and wonders in Jesus' name (Acts 4:30). We pray for the sick in Jesus’ name (Jms 5:14). We cast out devils and speak in tongues in Jesus’ name (Mk 16:17-18). We teach & preach in Jesus' name (Acts 4:17-18). Every knee should bow to Jesus (Phil 2:9-10). There is no salvation in any other name other than Jesus (Acts 4:12). You will be hated for Jesus' name (Acts 4:10). You will risk your life for Jesus' name (Acts 15:26). Persecuted for Jesus’ name (Acts 5:28). Jesus means YHWH-savior. All the Apostles baptized in Jesus' name. Yet, why do most Christians follow the Traditions of men rather that God’s Word by baptizing in a vague, nameless Trinity? “And whatsoever ye do in word or deed(baptism is a deed), DO ALL IN THE NAME OF THE LORD JESUS, giving thanks to God and the Father by him” (Col 3:17 KJV).

20.x: “..lo, I am with you always…”: Only omnipresent God can be everywhere present with all believers at all times until the end of the age. In Jn 14:17-18, Jesus promised: “I will not leave you comfortless(or “as orphans,” BSB, aka “without a FATHER”): I[Jesus] will come to you(as a HOLY SPIRIT),” or how can Jesus be with us always if not AS SPIRIT? That’s why Paul proclaimed: “the Lord is that Spirit: and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty” (2 Cor 3:17 KJV).
